Reivesti serves seven distinct roles in investment real estate, each with a different job to do: investors, cash buyers, wholesalers, Bird Dogs, private lenders, title companies and service providers.
Texas is a non-disclosure state with no state income tax and property tax administered county by county — three rules that change how every Texas investment property is underwritten.
Austin is a five-county investment market where most growth happens outside the county the city is in, and where Texas non-disclosure means comparable sale prices are never public record.
Understand a market before you choose a submarket. Reivesti gives investors metro-level buyer demand, liquidity and transaction velocity across U.S. markets.
Define acquisition criteria once — county, asset class, price band, condition, close timeline — and be matched against opportunities instead of sorting a blast list.
Disposition is a matching problem. Submit an opportunity into Reivesti Exchange once and reach buyers whose stated criteria already cover that county and price band.
Document property opportunities in the field — location, visible condition, photos, structured notes — and submit them with attribution tracked from submission through review.
Publish lending criteria — geography, asset class, leverage, term, deal size — so borrowers and operators reach you with deals that already qualify.
Claim a provider presence scoped to the counties you actually close in, so investors and operators transacting there can find and verify you.
Contractors, property managers, agents and other real estate service businesses join a provider network scoped to their category and the markets they actually serve.

Wave 0. This is the engine. Owned by the wholesale-specific city route per the 2026-07-31 intent-separation decision — NOT by the broad market page, which owns investment/market-research intent for the same city. The migration must preserve every one of the 33 legacy URLs — the legacy authority audit blocks retirement on all 127 URLs with Search Console rows for exactly this reason.

Wave 0. The assignment is explicit that Bird Dog must not be collapsed into a generic audience page, and the data agrees emphatically: one page outperforms 39 blog posts by 20x on clicks. Wave 1A (2026-08-01) supersedes the earlier 1:1 audience-page identity: the cluster is owned by the dedicated product page rebuilt at the legacy /nationwide-bird-dog-program path, and /for/bird-dogs supports it as the audience surface, re-cut to its own primary.

Wave 0. Position 18.43 is the best average position of any substantial non-brand cluster. Reassigned 2026-07-31 from role-wholesalers to a dedicated JV product page: an audience page must not absorb a proven product category (the exact product-category collapse assessApprovability() flags in the legacy module). Wave 1A (2026-08-01) built that page at the preserved legacy path /nationwide-joint-venture — the URL keeps its authority with no redirect at all; /submit-your-jv-wholesale-real-estate-deal/ remains preserved and cross-linked pending page-level query evidence.
The clearest evidence-backed gap in the whole registry: 17,496 impressions of practitioner-shaped demand with no page designed to serve it.

THE finding of this analysis. Google already shows Reivesti to this demand 47,936 times and Reivesti converts one click. The failure is format and position, not topic — the legacy pages sit on page six. Difficulty is high because Zillow, Redfin and LoopNet hold the head; the winnable surface is off-market inventory and geo intersections, not the bare head term.
Smaller first-party footprint than investment-properties but a far more defensible position: this is a category where holding inventory is the entire advantage.

Position 1.74 with zero clicks is the single most correctable finding in the dataset. The demand is tiny in the export but the SERP shows an entire competitive category, so the true size is Planner-dependent.
The owner page exists but targets "cash buyers real estate network". Confidence is low because the first-party read is an absence — this cluster is genuinely Planner-blocked for sizing.

Deliberately NOT assigned to the homepage. A homepage that tries to own a category term as well as the brand term owns neither well, and homepage overreach is one of the conflicts `ownership.ts` detects.
The highest-efficiency demand on the property and the least deliberately served. No page owns it; the clicks are incidental. Owned by /markets because that is where geographic resolution belongs.
Pairs with `wholesalers-directory` as the two sides of the network. Both are directory-shaped; neither exists.

Difficulty very-high: LendingTree and Nasdaq hold this on authority Reivesti will not match soon. Justified only as an authority asset feeding the money pages, and only because the legality table is a genuine differentiator. The blog evidence is a warning — do not repeat it.
The single strongest linkable-asset opportunity in the research. Saturated by volume, defended by nothing, and the differentiating measurement is a by-product of running the marketplace.

Deliberately deprioritised despite obvious volume. `proprietaryAdvantage: none` plus `difficulty: very-high` is the combination the scoring model is designed to demote, and it demotes this correctly. Included so the decision to skip it is recorded rather than silent.
Position 3.77 with zero clicks on 288 impressions warrants an investigation before a build. Two rows is not enough evidence to plan against, but it is enough to look at.
The strongest format signal in the entire observation set — a generic utility with no domain expertise holds the head term. Linkable asset first, money page second.
Low search demand today by construction. Justified on strategic-category value, and the scoring model scores it that way — 5 points of 100, honestly earned, not disguised as demand.
Owner exists as a role page. The directory *pages* — provider × state — are a separate programmatic family and belong in Wave 4, gated on enough verified providers to pass the originality gate.
Blocked on supply. A directory with no verified providers fails the originality gate, and shipping one anyway is the doorway-page failure this system exists to avoid.

Highest CPC category in the vertical and Reivesti has zero visibility in it. Entirely Planner-blocked for sizing — this is the cluster where "leave volume-dependent scoring unresolved" has the most consequence, and the roadmap places it in Wave 4 rather than guessing it into Wave 1.

A filtered cut of the Exchange rather than a new page family. Deliberately not given its own route — a separate distressed page would cannibalise both /investment-properties and /off-market-properties.
Explicitly deprioritised. The 30:1 terminology finding says the category should be named "investment properties" and rental treated as a cut beneath it — not as a competing top-level page.
Small first-party footprint. Sequenced after the calculator, which it depends on for its differentiator.
The strongest of the asset-class clusters on first-party CTR, and the one where the marketplace gap is most real.
Wave 5. Included for completeness of the asset-class family; not justified before inventory exists.
Wave 5. Recorded so the decision not to pursue commercial is explicit and evidenced rather than an omission.
The state-level investment-property pages are the worst-performing family on the property — two pages, 22,835 impressions, one click. The hub format replaces them rather than extending them.

Resolved 2026-07-31 by the intent-separation decision: the broad market page /markets/{state}/{market} owns investment and market-research intent for the city, and the wholesale-specific route owns wholesale intent. The former `metro-{market}-investment` sub-page is withdrawn — one market page per metro, cross-linked with its wholesale sibling under the coexistence contract in intent-separation.ts.

Four categories already work and are measured. Nothing in Waves 1–5 matters if the migration loses them. The legacy authority audit blocks retirement on all 127 URLs carrying Search Console rows, and this wave is that block expressed as a build plan.

Google already shows Reivesti to investment-property demand 47,936 times and Reivesti converts one click. This wave is not new demand acquisition — it is building pages capable of serving demand the property already receives and currently wastes.

Authority pages exist to route, not to attract. The property's own evidence is unambiguous — 39 blog posts produced 138 annual impressions each and 16 clicks in total. This wave publishes few pages, each with a single named destination, and none is justified on its own traffic.

Reivesti has published no calculator, index, dataset or report. Every competitor holding durable rankings has one. This wave builds the assets that earn links so the money pages can rank at all — it is the authority engine, not a traffic play.

Provider directories, the capital lane and asset-class expansion. Every one is gated on supply Reivesti does not have yet. This wave is dated by when the supply exists, not by when the pages could be written.
Asset class × market intersections and county-level geography. Only after the gate, the data and the editorial controls have been proven across Waves 0–4 on families that already have demand.
